case_title: P. Yuvaparakash v. State Rep. by Inspector of Police
statutory_provisions: IPC s.366A, POCSO Act s.6, s.10, JJ Act s.94
evidence_type: Medical, eyewitness, statement under Section 164 CrPC
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under POCSO Act, sentenced to life imprisonment
high_court_outcome: Confirmed conviction under POCSO Act, reduced sentence to 10 years, convicted under Prohibition of Child Marriage Act
neutral_facts: The accused and others allegedly kidnapped the victim, a 17-year-old girl, and engaged in sexual intercourse with her. The victim stated that she had known the accused and both loved each other, and had eloped voluntarily. The police traced the victim, and she provided a statement under Section 164 CrPC indicating she had consumed poison and was hospitalized due to her desire to live with the accused. The trial court convicted the accused under the POCSO Act and sentenced him to life imprisonment. The High Court confirmed the conviction but reduced the sentence to 10 years and also convicted him under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act. The Supreme Court overturned the conviction, finding that the prosecution failed to establish the victim's age as below 18 and that there was no evidence of penetrative sexual assault.
